rationale: PINS template-literal interpolation Uses (gap T3, kotlin K4 / scala G4 analog). TS semantics: `hi ${name} x${n + 1}` reads name and n — the substituted identifiers are expression usages of the enclosing function's symbols. BINDING SPELLING (2026-10-18): the interpolated PARAMETER reads are spelled `greet\u0000name` / `greet\u0000n` with meta.localBinding — a parameter is a name no declaration owns, so the family spelling states that; the rows still publish (this fixture's contract), only their target spelling changed. REVERTED 2026-10-18: the target is the WRITTEN name again (`param`, `name`, `n`), not the binding spelling — the differential counts a NUL-spelling as MISSING against a truth that derives the written name, so the spelling HID the row from the audit; the gate classifies the bare row honestly. UPDATED 2026-10-19 (D7 local-binding claim restored): the two parameter reads are now published with the binding spelling `greet\u0000name` / `greet\u0000n` + metadata.localBinding, because the imported/local binding claim kind now exists and the differential matcher strips the separator (`auditTarget`). The claim is verified by the spelling (bindOK), not resolved; the bare rows are FORBIDDEN so the same edge cannot be published twice. This supersedes the 2026-10-18 revert that kept written names while no claim kind existed.

expectRelationships.note: template interpolation of a PARAMETER: re-spelled to the family binding spelling (metadata.localBinding), verified by the arbiter from the spelling — bindOK column, never resolved
